True Dose-Toxicity and Dose-Response Scenarios

Source: R/oc_scenarios.R
oc_scenarios.Rd

Tabulate a list of scenarios, as given to the _multi simulation functions, with the true utility of every dose and the doses that are the true maximum tolerated dose (MTD) and the true optimal biological dose (OBD). The result is the truth against which oc_compare judges the designs, and it has print() and plot() methods.

Usage

oc_scenarios(
  scenarios,
  target,
  target_resp = NULL,
  tox_limit = target,
  psi00 = 40,
  psi11 = 60,
  resp_cor = 0,
  resp_cor_type = c("copula", "binary"),
  true_mtd = NULL,
  true_obd = NULL
)

Arguments

scenarios

List of scenarios. For a single agent, each element is a numeric vector of DLT probabilities or a list with the component p_true, and optionally p_resp (response probabilities) and name. For two drugs given together, p_true (and p_resp) are matrices with one row per level of drug A and one column per level of drug B. Either every scenario or none has p_resp. Names of the list are used when name is absent, and "Scenario 1", "Scenario 2", ... otherwise.

target

Numeric scalar. Target DLT probability; the true MTD is the dose whose DLT probability is closest to it.

target_resp

Numeric scalar or NULL. Lowest acceptable response probability, as target_resp of sim_boin12; a dose with a lower response probability cannot be the true OBD. Defaults to NULL, no such limit. The target_resp of sim_boin_et, the target response probability of BOIN-ET, is a different quantity.

tox_limit

Numeric scalar. Highest acceptable DLT probability; a dose with a higher DLT probability cannot be the true OBD. Defaults to target.

psi00, psi11

Numeric scalars. Utilities of a patient with neither a DLT nor a response and with both, on the scale where a response without a DLT scores 100 and a DLT without a response scores 0. Default to 40 and 60, as in sim_boin12.

resp_cor

Numeric scalar. Correlation between the DLT and the response, used for the probabilities of the four outcomes. Defaults to 0, independence.

resp_cor_type

Character scalar. How resp_cor is read, as in sim_boin12: "copula" (the default), the correlation of the latent normal variables, or "binary", the correlation of the two binary outcomes.

true_mtd, true_obd

NULL (the default) or a list with one element per scenario, in the order of scenarios or named by the scenarios, giving the true MTDs or OBDs directly when the definition of an article differs from the one used here: a vector of dose levels for a single agent, a two-column matrix of the levels of drug A and drug B for a combination, or NULL for the computed doses. An empty vector means no such dose.

Value

A data frame of class c("oc_scenarios", "data.frame") with one row per scenario and dose (or combination) and the columns

scenario

Factor of the scenario names, in the order given.

dose

Dose level, or dose_a and dose_b for a combination.

p_true

True DLT probability.

p_resp, utility

True response probability and utility, when the scenarios have response probabilities.

true_mtd

Logical, the dose is a true MTD.

true_obd

Logical, the dose is a true OBD, when the scenarios have response probabilities.

The arguments are kept as attributes, with type ("single" or "combination") and dims (the number of doses, or the numbers of levels of the two drugs).

Details

The utility of a dose is 100 * Pr(response, no DLT) + psi00 * Pr(neither) + psi11 * Pr(both). The true MTDs are all the doses whose DLT probability is closest to target (several when tied). The true OBDs are all the doses with the highest utility among the doses whose DLT probability is at most tox_limit and, when target_resp is given, whose response probability is at least target_resp; a scenario may have none. Ties are decided with a tolerance of 1e-10.

Some articles use other definitions, for example Lin et al. (2020), who count every dose within 3 points of the highest utility as an OBD; give such doses through true_obd.

References

Lin, R., Zhou, Y., Yan, F., Li, D. and Yuan, Y. (2020). BOIN12: Bayesian optimal interval phase I/II trial design for utility-based dose finding in immunotherapy and targeted therapies. JCO Precision Oncology, 4, 1393-1402. doi:10.1200/PO.20.00257

See also

oc_results, oc_compare, print.oc_scenarios, plot.oc_scenarios

Examples

truth <- oc_scenarios(
  list(
    "Scenario 1" = list(p_true = c(0.05, 0.12, 0.27, 0.35, 0.50),
                        p_resp = c(0.20, 0.35, 0.36, 0.37, 0.38)),
    "Scenario 2" = list(p_true = c(0.05, 0.12, 0.27, 0.35, 0.50),
                        p_resp = c(0.01, 0.05, 0.30, 0.60, 0.60))
  ),
  target = 0.35, target_resp = 0.25
)
truth
#> True scenarios: 2 scenario(s), 5 doses 
#> True MTD: DLT probability closest to 0.35 
#> True OBD: highest utility among the doses with DLT probability <= 0.35 and response probability >= 0.25 
#> Utilities: 100 (response, no DLT), 40 (neither), 60 (both), 0 (DLT, no response)
#> 
#> Scenario 1
#>             1    2    3    4    5
#> p_true   0.05 0.12 0.27 0.35 0.50
#> p_resp   0.20 0.35 0.36 0.37 0.38
#> utility  50.0 56.2 50.8 48.2 42.8
#> true MTD                   *     
#> true OBD         *               
#> 
#> Scenario 2
#>             1    2    3    4    5
#> p_true   0.05 0.12 0.27 0.35 0.50
#> p_resp   0.01 0.05 0.30 0.60 0.60
#> utility  38.6 38.2 47.2 62.0 56.0
#> true MTD                   *     
#> true OBD                   *
